crons.name: morning-edition
crons.message:
⚡ EXEC DISCIPLINE: run any `python3 <path>` command exactly as written — a bare invocation, nothing appended, no shell wrapping, no chaining with other commands, no output redirection, no exit-code capture. Scripts always print one JSON line to stdout with a `status` field (ok/error/degraded); parse that final line to decide what to do. openclaw 2026.4.11 rejects complex shell invocations before they run. Generate the morning news digest. Run: python3 ~/.openclaw/news-digest-workspace/scripts/fetch-and-rank.py. This fetches all RSS feeds and LinkedIn updates, ranks them against the preference model at preferences/model.json, and writes cache/ranked-<date>.json. Read the ranked output. Select the top 15-20 items. For each item, write a one-sentence extended headline explaining why it matters. Group items by topic category (🤖 AI & Tech, 💰 Economics, 🌍 World, 🏛️ US Policy, 🔗 LinkedIn, 📋 Also Noted). 

You MUST write TWO files. The fleet-delivery script reads the first; a legacy chunked-text fallback uses the second.

FILE 1 — cache/morning-items.json (structured, authoritative for Telegram delivery):
A JSON array of item objects, one per selected item, in the order they should be delivered. Each object has:
  {"num": <1..N>,                         // sequential, matches /like N
   "category": "✍️ Category name",       // with leading emoji, e.g. "🤖 AI & Tech"
   "extended_headline": "<1 sentence>",   // your rewritten headline + why it matters
   "title": "<raw article title>",        // for reference
   "url": "<canonical url>",
   "source_label": "<source display>",    // e.g. "Reuters", "NYT World", "LinkedIn Message"
   "topics": [<topic tags from ranked file>]}
Write the file atomically. If you can't open it, stop — don't continue to FILE 2.

FILE 2 — cache/morning-brief-ready.txt (plain text fallback, human-readable):
Same items rendered as plain text with headings and the inline-command form (👍 /like_N    👎 /dislike_N    📖 /more_N). End with a line: 🐛 {total} items · {source_count} sources · Reply inline or with /ask [topic]. This file exists only as a fallback; when morning-items.json is fresh, fleet-delivery ignores this.

For LinkedIn message thread items (source=linkedin, source_label contains 'Message'), the title already contains the sender and the summary is an LLM-generated thread summary. Use those as the headline fields.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT send to Telegram. The host-cron morning-fleet-deliver (fires at 12:00 UTC = 5:00 AM PT) reads morning-items.json and sends each item as its own message with 👍/👎/📖 inline keyboard buttons via the NEWSDIGEST_BOT_TOKEN. Your job ends when both cache files are written. Update your status file with the items count and any feed errors.

crons.name: preference-update
crons.message: ⚡ EXEC DISCIPLINE: run any `python3 <path>` command exactly as written — a bare invocation, nothing appended, no shell wrapping, no chaining with other commands, no output redirection, no exit-code capture. Scripts always print one JSON line to stdout with a `status` field (ok/error/degraded); parse that final line to decide what to do. openclaw 2026.4.11 rejects complex shell invocations before they run. Process today's engagement signals and update the preference model. Run: python3 ~/.openclaw/news-digest-workspace/scripts/update-preferences.py. This reads new entries from preferences/engagement.jsonl, applies multiplicative weight updates (thumbs_up: topic ×1.1 source ×1.05, thumbs_down: topic ×0.85 source ×0.95, expand: topic ×1.05), clamps weights to safe ranges, and writes updated model to preferences/model.json. If there are no new engagement events, skip the update silently. Update your status file with the number of events processed and otherwise, return EXACTLY the empty string (zero bytes, no narration — not even "NO output", "Done", "all clear", or a status summary). Any text you emit is logged and charges tokens even when no Telegram message is sent.
